content: 1. When guanfacine is coadministered with certain agents, its dosage should be reduced to half of the recommended dose. Specific recommendations for immediate-release guanfacine are not available. 2. Histrelin increases the toxicity of erythromycin stearate by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely, as this combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 3. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of hydrocortisone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Hydroxyzine increases the toxicity of erythromycin stearate by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely, as this combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 5. Erythromycin stearate decreases the levels or effects of ifosfamide by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. The use of a CYP3A4 inhibitor may reduce ifosfamide metabolism, potentially diminishing its therapeutic effects. 6. Erythromycin stearate and iloperidone both prolong the QTc interval. Iloperidone increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Iloperidone, as a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor, may elevate plasma levels of drugs primarily metabolized by CYP3A4. 7. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of imatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of inhaled indacaterol by modulating P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4 activities. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs that prolong the QTc interval may increase the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 9. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of indinavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of irinotecan and liposomal irinotecan by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of isavuconazonium sulfate by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of isradipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Istradefylline increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. At 40 mg/day, istradefylline increased peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials, but this effect was not observed at 20 mg/day. 14. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of itraconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of ivacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce ivacaftor dose if coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Ivacaftor also increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. 16. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of ivermectin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of ivosidenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase ivosidenib plasma concentrations, raising the risk of QTc prolongation. 18. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of ketoconazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Ketoconazole also increases erythromycin stearate levels by the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of lapatinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both erythromycin stearate and lapatinib prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 20. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of larotrectinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Lencapavir increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Lencapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase CYP3A4 substrate levels initiated within nine months after its last subcutaneous dose, potentially increasing the risk of adverse reactions. 22. Erythromycin stearate and lenvatinib both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenvatinib prescribing information recommends close ECG monitoring when coadministered with QT-prolonging drugs. 23. Leuprolide increases the toxicity of erythromycin stearate by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely, as this combination increases the risk of torsades de pointes. 24. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of levamlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A inhibitors increases systemic exposure to amlodipine and may require dose reduction. Monitor for symptoms of hypotension and edema. 25. Erythromycin stearate and levofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 26. Levoketoconazole increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Erythromycin stearate also increases levoketoconazole levels by the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Erythromycin stearate decreases the levels or effects of levonorgestrel oral/ethinyl estradiol/ferrous bisglycinate by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of loperamide by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Lorlatinib decreases erythromycin stearate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of lumateperone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce lumateperone dose to 21 mg/day if coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 31. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of lurasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. The manufacturer recommends reducing the starting dose of lurasidone to 20 mg/day and the maximum daily dose to 80 mg when coadministered with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. 32. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of maraviroc by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Initiation of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may require a decreased mavacamten dose. 34. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of mavorizxafor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Mavorizxafor and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Monitor QTc during treatment in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation. 35. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of mefloquine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Erythromycin stearate decreases the levels or effects of mestranol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Erythromycin stearate also increases mestranol levels by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Erythromycin stearate and methadone both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 38. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of methylprednisolone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of mifepristone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both mifepristone and erythromycin stearate prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 40. Mipomersen and erythromycin stearate both have the potential to increase hepatic enzymes. Monitor liver function tests (LFTs) and use caution. 41. Mitotane decreases erythromycin stearate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4; monitor for possible dosage adjustments when coadministered with CYP3A4 substrates. 42. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of mitoxantrone by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Erythromycin stearate increases the toxicity of momelotinib by inhibiting OATP1B1/B3 transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. Elevated momelotinib plasma concentrations may increase the risk of adverse reactions. 44. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of montelukast by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of naldemedine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor for potential adverse effects if coadministered with P-gp inhibitors. 46. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of nelfinavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of neomycin PO by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Erythromycin stearate decreases the levels or effects of niacin by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of nifedipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Consider initiating nifedipine at the lowest dose available if given concomitantly. 50. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of nilotinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of nimodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels of nintedanib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Modify therapy and monitor closely. If adverse effects occur, management may require interruption, dose reduction, or discontinuation of therapy. 53. Nirmatrelvir increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor for increased erythromycin adverse effects, including QTc prolongation. 54. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases erythromycin stearate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor for increased erythromycin adverse effects, including QTc prolongation. 55. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of nitrendipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of norgestrel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic concentrations of norgestrel, potentially increasing the risk of adverse effects. 57. Erythromycin stearate and ofloxacin both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 58. Erythromycin stearate increases the levels or effects of oliceridine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. If concomitant use is necessary, less frequent oliceridine dosing may be required. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and titrate subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing oliceridine dosage until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 59. Erythromycin stearate and olodaterol inhaled both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Drugs that prolong the QTc interval may potentiate the effects of beta-2 agonists on the cardiovascular system, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. 60. Osilodrostat and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Osimertinib and erythromycin stearate both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Conduct periodic monitoring with ECGs and electrolytes in patients.
